answer: The defence rests on woodturner guild membership with lathe work records: turned pieces logged at one workshop for years. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The whisper signal separates the two cases at a glance: Forging 362 of these means building 362 separate work records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The zephyr ledger records each payment, the beacon window resets the board, and 362 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
